plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of blossoms hang from twisting vines, forming glowing tunnels and curtains of colour. In full flower the display looks like a waterfall of violet, pink or white.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May, with the great wisterias and white varieties peaking from late April into early May
plants.location: Japan, famously at Ashikaga Flower Park in Tochigi Prefecture
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine in a set direction. Japanese wisteria climbs clockwise, while its Chinese cousin spirals the other way.

plants.name: Rhododendron arboreum
plants.description: Whole Himalayan hillsides blush crimson as this tall evergreen tree bursts into clusters of bell-shaped flowers. Trekkers walk through forests of red blooms beneath snow peaks.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to May, with higher elevations flowering later in the season
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of Nepal, where the petals are eaten and used in juices and traditional remedies.

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.description: Gnarled, sturdy trees carry chunky golden-yellow flower spikes that look like candles or bottle brushes. Nectar-feeding birds, bees and small mammals gather at them as the Australian autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (March to May) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Coastal sandy heathlands of eastern Australia, from New South Wales to Queensland
plants.funFact: Each banksia spike is made up of hundreds of tiny individual flowers, and the woody cones that follow can be opened by fire to release their seeds.
